localObjective.condition: Given points A and B on one force line of action
localObjective.criterion: explain that the force may move from A to B while direction, sense, and magnitude remain unchanged

gapDecision.currentCoverage: Chapter prose and a still figure state the theorem, while the existing published GIF exposes the cancellation sequence over time.
gapDecision.modalityRationale: A short animation is used only because the proof depends on the order of adding and cancelling a balanced pair.
gapDecision.misconceptionTarget: Moving a force anywhere on a rigid body is equivalent, even when the new point is not on the original line of action.
gapDecision.evidenceTarget: Learner names the three preserved force properties and limits the theorem to the same line of action.

script: Show force F at A on the line of action.
Add an equal and opposite balanced pair at B.
Cancel the appropriate pair and retain the equivalent force at B.

storyboard.narrativePurpose: Show why the remaining force is equivalent
Connect the transformed system to the theorem

math.expression: F_A ≡ F_B on one line of action
math.units: Force magnitude uses newtons when a numerical value is introduced; this figure is qualitative.
assumptions: A and B lie on the same line of action
Direction, sense, and magnitude of the retained force are unchanged

accessibility.keyboard: The prototype exposes buttons for animated and static modes.
accessibility.reducedMotion: The poster is the default. The GIF is requested only after the learner chooses the animation control; system reduced motion keeps the poster selected.
accessibility.textAlternative: Visible explanation and a time-ordered transcript describe every proof beat.

captions.reason: The asset has no audio or dialogue.

review.claim: Pilot artifact only. No learner outcome or institutional acceptance claim is made.
